title: CRLR/441/2021 of SHADRANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.441 of 2021
Shadrana ...Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and another ...Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. T.C. Agarwal, D.A.G. for the State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to an order
dated 09.12.2021, passed in Case No. 128 of 2021,
Shardran Vs. Khusnaseeb, by the court of Judge, Family
Court, Laksar ("the case"). By it, an application for interim
maintenance of the revisionist was allowed and the private
respondent was directed to pay Rs.2000/- per month as
interim maintenance to the revisionist.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. It appears that the revisionist filed an application
under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
("the Code") seeking maintenance from the private
respondent Khusnaseeb, her husband. According to the
revisionist, she and the private respondent were married on
10.11.2016. But, after the marriage, she was harassed and

2
tortured in her in-law's house. Finally, she was divorced.
She is staying in her parental house. She is not able to
maintain herself. The private respondent earns Rs.15,000/-
per month. This application is a basis of the case.
4. In the case, an application for interim
maintenance was filed by the revisionist. It has been
objected to by the private respondent. He has rebutted all
the allegations. According to the private respondent, he had
married earlier, but his wife expired leaving behind two
children, one of whom is physically challenged. In order to
look after his children, he married again, but the revisionist
left him.
5. After hearing the parties, by the impugned order,
an application for interim maintenance filed by the
revisionist has been allowed. The private respondent has
been directed to pay Rs.2,000/- per month, as interim
maintenance, to the revisionist. It is impugned herein.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would submit
that Rs.2000/- per month interim maintenance is much
inadequate. It cannot help the revisionist to survive.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
private respondent would submit that the private
respondent is simply a labourer. He has three children to
look after. Two from the earlier wife and one from the
revisionist. It is submitted that one of his children is

3
physically challenged. Therefore, learned counsel would
submit that the amount of maintenance which has been
awarded as an interim maintenance is not inadequate.
8. Impugned order has been passed at the stage of
interim maintenance. The parties have yet to enter into the
trial of the case. They have an opportunity to adduce
evidence with regard to their financial resources, liabilities,
responsibilities etc.
9. In the instant case, a certificate from the
Tehsildar was also filed by the private respondent revealing
his income as Rs.5,500/- per month. At the time of
arguments, on behalf of the revisionist it is also argued that
how could the Tehsildar give income certificate? Fact
remains that though the private respondent has filed such a
certificate, the court below assessed his monthly income at
Rs.8,000/- to Rs.9,000/- Based on it, Rs.2000/- per month
interim maintenance was awarded to the revisionist.
10. It is not disputed that the private respondent
also maintains three minor children. One of them, according
to learned counsel for the private respondent is physically
challenged. Undoubtedly, Rs.2000/- is too less amount to
maintain, but then, it is always relative depending upon the
status, financial resources and placement in the society of
the parties etc.

4
11. In the instant case, it has been observed by the
court below that the income of the private respondent is
Rs.8,000/- to Rs.9,000/- per month. Having considered the
family, which the private respondent is to look after, this
Court is of the view that the amount which has been
awarded cannot be termed as inadequate at this stage.
Accordingly, the revision deserves to be dismissed.
12. The revision is dismissed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 21.11.2022
Jitendra
